lead: A neighbourhood of blocks on the slopes of Collserola, with a park, Olympic facilities and the area's major hospital.
text: It grew out of the Parc de la Vall d'Hebron housing estate, built in 1968 on former estates of the old municipality of Horta, following the 1953 Plan Comarcal. After the 1992 Olympic Games the area was reorganised, the estate was extended and some sports facilities were allocated to it. The Olympic extension also brought new homes, and its landmarks include the Pavelló de la República.

It is a small neighbourhood, with 6,087 inhabitants in 0.74 km², made up of residential blocks at the corner of the Ronda de Dalt and Passeig de la Vall d'Hebron, with the Parc de la Vall d'Hebron as its landmark. The large hospital complex that bears its name is in the neighbouring Montbau, north of the Ronda de Dalt. If you are selling, the average sale price (3,866 €/m² in 2025) is 12% above the Horta-Guinardó average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 309,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Horta-Guinardó (5th of 11 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (976 €/month) is 7% above the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Estates of residential blocks built from the late 1960s.
